source.text: Ἰησοῦς δὲ πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου ὑπέστρεψεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἤγετο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.

records.literal_gloss: Jesus then full of [the] Spirit Holy returned from the Jordan, and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness \v 2 days forty being tempted by the devil.

en.L: And Jesus, full of [the] Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness \v 2 for forty days, being tempted by the devil.
en.B: Jesus came back from the Jordan full of the Holy Spirit, and the Spirit led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} through the wilderness \v 2 for forty days, while the devil put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the test.
en.R: Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back from the Jordan River. The Spirit led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} around in the desert \v 2 for forty days. All that time the devil tried to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do wrong.

es.L: Y Jesús, lleno de Espíritu Santo, volvió del Jordán, y era conducido por el Espíritu en el desierto \v 2 durante cuarenta días, siendo tentado por el diablo.
es.B: Jesús volvió del Jordán lleno del Espíritu Santo, y el Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} guiaba por el desierto \v 2 durante cuarenta días, mientras el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ponía a prueba.
es.R: Jesús estaba lleno del Espíritu Santo cuando regresó del río Jordán. El Espíritu {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó de un lugar a otro por el desierto \v 2 durante cuarenta días. Todo ese tiempo el diablo intentaba que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hiciera algo malo.

fr.L: Et Jésus, plein d’Esprit Saint, revint du Jourdain, et il était conduit par l’Esprit dans le désert \v 2 pendant quarante jours, tenté par le diable.
fr.B: Jésus revint du Jourdain, rempli de l’Esprit Saint, et l’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} conduisait à travers le désert \v 2 pendant quarante jours, tandis que le diable {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettait à l’épreuve.
fr.R: Jésus était rempli de l’Esprit Saint quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est revenu du fleuve Jourdain. L’Esprit {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a conduit dans le désert \v 2 pendant quarante jours. Pendant tout ce temps, le diable a essayé de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pousser à faire le mal.

sw.L: Basi Yesu, akiwa amejawa na Roho Mtakatifu, alirejea kutoka Yordani, na alikuwa akiongozwa na Roho katika nyika \v 2 kwa siku arobaini, akijaribiwa na Ibilisi.
sw.B: Yesu alirejea kutoka Yordani akiwa amejawa na Roho Mtakatifu, na Roho akawa anamwongoza katika nyika \v 2 kwa siku arobaini, huku Ibilisi akimjaribu.
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa amejawa na Roho Mtakatifu aliporudi kutoka Mto Yordani. Roho alimwongoza huku na huko jangwani \v 2 kwa siku arobaini. Wakati wote huo Ibilisi alijaribu kumshawishi atende mabaya.

decisions.choice: was led by the Spirit in the wilderness: the Spirit kept leading him while he was in the wilderness, through the forty days
alternatives: was led by the Spirit into the wilderness
decisions.reason: The Greek says "in" the wilderness, not "into", and the verb is in the imperfect tense: the leading went on during the whole time. The Spirit who came on Jesus at his baptism (3:22) now guides him.

decisions.choice: being tempted: put to the test by one who wants him to fail
decisions.reason: The verb means both to test and to tempt. The devil is the one doing it, and he wants Jesus to turn from God's way (4:13).

decisions.choice: forty days in the wilderness: as Israel was tested forty years in the wilderness
alternatives: a round number with no further meaning
decisions.reason: Jesus answers each test with words from Deuteronomy 6-8, where Moses reminds Israel of its forty years in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:2). Moses and Elijah also went forty days without food (Exodus 34:28; 1 Kings 19:8).

decisions.choice: the devil: the slanderer, God's enemy, also called Satan
alternatives: an evil impulse within a person
decisions.reason: The word means "slanderer". The Greek Old Testament uses it for Satan, the accuser (Job 1:6; Zechariah 3:1).

decisions.choice: tried to make him do wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what tempting means, as Matthew 4:1 does.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word, as in 3:2. It was dry, empty land, not necessarily sand.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} on the clitic pronouns
decisions.reason: Wherever the English marks a pronoun for Jesus, the Spanish clitic standing before the verb takes the span too, as the stressed pronouns (él, ti, mí) do. A clitic joined to the end of a verb ("llevándolo") cannot take a capital and has none, and Spanish leaves out many subject pronouns the English needs, so Spanish has fewer spans in this chapter.

decisions.choice: el desierto
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the wild, empty land at every level, as in Matthew; the English says "wilderness" (L, B) and "desert" (R), but Spanish "desierto" covers both.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, including the history Jesus retells in 4:25-27. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: l’Esprit Saint; le diable; le désert at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Mark: "l’Esprit Saint" and "le diable" in every book, and "le désert", which in French means empty wild land, not only sand, so it serves both the English "wilderness" and Readable's "desert". Literal says "plein d’Esprit Saint" without the article, as the Greek has none.

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb (alimwongoza, akimjaribu), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so only free pronouns (yeye, wewe, mimi) and possessives (wake, yake, yangu) carry the deity_pronoun span. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English in this chapter.

decisions.choice: nyika (L, B); jangwa (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: "nyika" is open, empty wild country, which is what the Greek means; Readable uses the everyday "jangwa", as the English Readable says "desert".

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ συντελεσθεισῶν αὐτῶν ἐπείνασεν.

records.literal_gloss: And not he ate nothing in the days those, and having been completed they he was hungry.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ate nothing in those days, and when they were completed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.
en.B: He went without food the whole time, and when the days were over, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.
en.R: He did not eat anything during those days. So at the end of that time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very hungry.

es.L: Y no comió nada en aquellos días, y cuando se cumplieron, tuvo hambre.
es.B: No probó alimento en todo ese tiempo, y cuando terminaron aquellos días, tuvo hambre.
es.R: No comió nada durante esos días. Por eso, al final de ese tiempo tenía mucha hambre.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne mangea rien en ces jours-là, et quand ils furent achevés, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut faim.
fr.B: Il ne mangea rien pendant tout ce temps et, quand ces jours furent passés, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut faim.
fr.R: Il n’a rien mangé pendant ces jours-là. Alors, à la fin de ce temps, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait très faim.

sw.L: Na hakula chochote katika siku zile, na zilipotimia, aliona njaa.
sw.B: Hakula chakula chochote muda wote huo, na siku hizo zilipoisha, alikuwa na njaa.
sw.R: Hakula kitu chochote katika siku hizo. Kwa hiyo, mwishoni mwa muda huo alikuwa na njaa sana.

decisions.choice: ate nothing: a complete fast
decisions.reason: The Greek doubles the negative ("not ... nothing") for emphasis.

decisions.choice: when they were completed, he was hungry: the devil's first test comes at his weakest point
alternatives: he was hungry only at the end
decisions.reason: Luke links the hunger to the first test, which is about bread (4:3).

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ τῷ λίθῳ τούτῳ ἵνα γένηται ἄρτος.

records.literal_gloss: Said then to him the devil, If Son you are of the God, speak to the stone this that it become bread.

en.L: And the devil said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are [the] Son of God, tell this stone that it should become bread."
en.B: The devil said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the Son of God, order this stone to turn into bread."
en.R: The devil said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are really the Son of God, make this stone turn into bread."

es.L: Y el diablo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si eres [el] Hijo de Dios, di a esta piedra que se convierta en pan».
es.B: El diablo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si eres el Hijo de Dios, ordena a esta piedra que se convierta en pan».
es.R: El diablo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Si de verdad eres el Hijo de Dios, haz que esta piedra se convierta en pan».

fr.L: Et le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es [le] Fils de Dieu, dis à cette pierre qu’elle devienne du pain. »
fr.B: Le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le Fils de Dieu, ordonne à cette pierre de se changer en pain. »
fr.R: Le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es vraiment le Fils de Dieu, transforme cette pierre en pain. »

sw.L: Na Ibilisi akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, sema na jiwe hili ili liwe mkate."
sw.B: Ibilisi alimwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, liamuru jiwe hili ligeuke kuwa mkate."
sw.R: Ibilisi alimwambia, "Kama kweli {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, fanya jiwe hili ligeuke kuwa mkate."

decisions.choice: if you are the Son of God: taking up what God has just said (3:22), and inviting Jesus to prove it
alternatives: since you are the Son of God, with no doubt implied
decisions.reason: The form of the Greek condition assumes the statement for the sake of argument. The devil does not deny that Jesus is God's Son; he tries to get him to use that status for himself. The genealogy has just ended "son of Adam, son of God" (3:38).

decisions.choice: this stone: one stone, pointed out
decisions.reason: Luke has the singular; Matthew has "these stones ... loaves".

decisions.choice: really
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the challenge in the "if", as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος.

records.literal_gloss: And answered to him the Jesus, It has been written that Not on bread alone will live the man.

en.L: And Jesus answered him, "It is written, '{{gender:A person|Man}} will not live on bread alone.'"
en.B: Jesus answered him, "It stands written, '{{gender:A person|Man}} does not live on bread alone.'"
en.R: Jesus answered, "The Scriptures say, 'People need more than bread to live.'"

es.L: Y Jesús le respondió: «Está escrito: “No de pan solo vivirá {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}}”».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «La Escritura dice: “{{gender:El ser humano|El hombre}} no vive solo de pan”».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Las Escrituras dicen: “La gente necesita algo más que pan para vivir”».

fr.L: Et Jésus lui répondit : « Il est écrit : “{{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} ne vivra pas de pain seul.” »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Il est écrit : “{{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} ne vit pas uniquement de pain.” »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Les Écritures disent : “Pour vivre, les gens n’ont pas seulement besoin de pain.” »

sw.L: Na Yesu akamjibu, "Imeandikwa kwamba, 'Mwanadamu hataishi kwa mkate peke yake.'"
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Binadamu haishi kwa mkate peke yake.'"
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Maandiko yanasema, 'Watu wanahitaji zaidi ya mkate ili waishi.'"

decisions.choice: It is written: Deuteronomy 8:3, where God fed Israel with manna to teach them to depend on his word
decisions.reason: Moses tells Israel that God let them go hungry and then fed them, so that they would learn that people live by every word from the LORD's mouth. Jesus is hungry like Israel but trusts God instead of providing for himself.

decisions.choice: it is written: it stands written and still has authority
decisions.reason: The perfect tense means a past act whose result remains. Jesus answers each test with Scripture (4:8, 4:12).

decisions.choice: the man: a human being, anyone
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being.

decisions.choice: the quotation ends with "bread alone" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: adds "but by every word of God"
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts end the quotation here. Many later ones add the rest of the line from Deuteronomy 8:3, as Matthew 4:4 has it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:A person|Man}} (L, B); People (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek means any human being. The traditional "Man" is offered as the alternative; Readable's "People" is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: People need more than bread to live
alternatives: Man shall not live on bread alone
decisions.reason: Readable says the point plainly, as in Matthew 4:4.

decisions.choice: {{gender:el ser humano|el hombre}} (L, B); la gente (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish has the same two wordings as English: "el hombre" in the older sense of any human being, or "el ser humano" (meaning decision m3). Readable says "la gente", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: Está escrito (L); La Escritura dice (B); Las Escrituras dicen (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: Literal keeps the Greek perfect; Balanced and Readable say plainly that Scripture speaks, and the present tense keeps the sense that it still has authority (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:L’être humain|L’homme}} (L, B); les gens (R)
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (m3). French "l’homme" is read as "the man" more and more, so the inclusive default says it plainly and the traditional wording is the alternative, as in English. Readable's "les gens" is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: mwanadamu (L); binadamu (B), no gender setting
decisions.reason: Both words already mean any human being, man or woman (meaning decision m3), so Swahili has no second wording for the English gender setting to choose.

decisions.choice: Imeandikwa (L); Maandiko yanasema (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording: Literal keeps the Greek perfect; Balanced and Readable say that Scripture speaks, in the present, since its word still stands (meaning decision m2).

source.text: Καὶ ἀναγαγὼν αὐτὸν ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐν στιγμῇ χρόνου·

records.literal_gloss: And having led up him he showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

en.L: And leading {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up, he showed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
en.B: Then the devil took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up high, and in a single instant he let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} see every kingdom of the world.
en.R: Next the devil took Jesus up to a high place. In just a moment he showed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} every kingdom in the world.

es.L: Y llevándolo arriba, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mostró todos los reinos del mundo en un instante de tiempo.
es.B: Luego el diablo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevó a lo alto, y en un solo instante {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hizo ver todos los reinos del mundo.
es.R: Después el diablo llevó a Jesús a un lugar alto. En un momento {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mostró todos los reinos del mundo.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ayant emmené en haut, il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} montra tous les royaumes du monde habité en un instant de temps.
fr.B: Puis le diable {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmena sur une hauteur et, en un seul instant, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} fit voir tous les royaumes du monde.
fr.R: Ensuite, le diable a emmené Jésus dans un endroit élevé. En un instant, il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a montré tous les royaumes du monde.

sw.L: Na akiisha kumpandisha juu, alimwonyesha falme zote za dunia katika kitambo kimoja cha wakati.
sw.B: Kisha Ibilisi alimpeleka juu, na kwa kitambo kimoja akamwonyesha falme zote za dunia.
sw.R: Baadaye Ibilisi alimpeleka Yesu mahali pa juu. Mara moja akamwonyesha falme zote za dunia.

decisions.choice: in a moment of time: in an instant, as in a vision
decisions.reason: No place on earth could show every kingdom; Luke stresses that it happened in a flash.

decisions.choice: the world: the inhabited world, the nations and their rulers
decisions.reason: Luke uses the word for the inhabited earth, as in 2:1, where Augustus ruled it.

decisions.choice: having led him up (SBLGNT), with no mountain named
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts do not name a mountain here; many later ones add it from Matthew 4:8. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the devil
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject so that the reader can tell the devil from Jesus.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Σοὶ δώσω τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἅπασαν καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐμοὶ παραδέδοται καὶ ᾧ ἂν θέλω δίδωμι αὐτήν·

records.literal_gloss: And said to him the devil, To you I will give the authority this all and the glory of them, for to me it has been handed over and to whom if I wish I give it;

en.L: And the devil said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I will give all this authority and their glory, for it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
en.B: And the devil said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} power over all of them, and all their glory. It has been handed over to me, and I hand it on to whoever I please.
en.R: The devil said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the right to rule all of them, and their glory will be {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} too. It has all been given to me, so I can give it to whoever I like.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo el diablo: «A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré toda esta autoridad y la gloria de ellos, porque se me ha entregado a mí, y yo la doy a quien desee.
es.B: Y el diablo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Te daré poder sobre todos ellos, y toda su gloria. Se me ha entregado, y yo se lo paso a quien me plazca.
es.R: El diablo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Te daré el derecho de gobernar a todos ellos, y su gloria también será {{deity_pronoun:tuya|Tuya}}. Todo eso me lo han dado a mí, así que puedo dárselo a quien yo quiera.

fr.L: Et le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « À {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je donnerai toute cette autorité et leur gloire, car elle m’a été livrée, et je la donne à qui je veux.
fr.B: Le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donnerai le pouvoir sur tous ces royaumes, et toute leur gloire. Ce pouvoir m’a été remis, et je le transmets à qui il me plaît.
fr.R: Le diable {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Je vais {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donner le droit de régner sur tous ces royaumes, et leur gloire sera à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} aussi. Tout cela m’a été donné, alors je peux le donner à qui je veux.

sw.L: Na Ibilisi akamwambia, "Nitakupa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} mamlaka haya yote na utukufu wa [falme] hizo, kwa sababu yamekabidhiwa kwangu, nami nayatoa kwa yeyote ninayemtaka.
sw.B: Ibilisi alimwambia, "Nitakupa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} mamlaka juu ya falme hizi zote, pamoja na utukufu wake wote. Nimekabidhiwa mamlaka hayo, nami nampa yeyote ninayependa.
sw.R: Ibilisi alimwambia, "Nitakupa mamlaka ya kutawala falme hizi zote, na utukufu wake utakuwa {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} pia. Vyote hivi nimepewa mimi, kwa hiyo naweza kumpa yeyote ninayemtaka.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and power to rule
decisions.reason: The devil offers rule over the kingdoms he has just shown.

decisions.choice: glory: their splendor, wealth and honor
decisions.reason: Here the word is used of the kingdoms' splendor, as in Matthew 4:8.

decisions.choice: it has been handed over to me: the devil's claim, which Jesus does not dispute but refuses
alternatives: a plain lie with no truth in it
a true statement of the devil's right
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the New Testament calls Satan the ruler of this world (John 12:31; 2 Corinthians 4:4; 1 John 5:19). Yet Scripture says that God gives kingdoms to whomever he wishes (Daniel 4:17). The passive "has been handed over" leaves the giver unnamed.

decisions.choice: the right to rule all of them
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of authority is offered.

decisions.choice: and their glory will be yours too
decisions.reason: Readable repeats the promise with a verb so the short phrase is easy to follow.

decisions.choice: mamlaka (L, B); mamlaka ya kutawala (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this authority, the right and power to rule (meaning decision m1). "Haki" is kept for righteousness, so the English Readable's "the right to rule" becomes "mamlaka ya kutawala".

source.text: σὺ οὖν ἐὰν προσκυνήσῃς ἐνώπιον ἐμοῦ, ἔσται σοῦ πᾶσα.

records.literal_gloss: You therefore if you worship before me, will be yours all.

en.L: You, then, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} worship before me, all of it will be {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}."
en.B: So if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will bow down to me in worship, all of it will belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will just bow down and worship me, it will all belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Tú, pues, si {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} postras en adoración delante de mí, todo será {{deity_pronoun:tuyo|Tuyo}}».
es.B: Así que, si {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} inclinas ante mí para adorarme, todo será {{deity_pronoun:tuyo|Tuyo}}».
es.R: Si solo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} arrodillas y me adoras, todo será {{deity_pronoun:tuyo|Tuyo}}».

fr.L: Toi donc, si {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} prosternes devant moi, tout sera à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. »
fr.B: Si donc {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} prosternes devant moi pour m’adorer, tout cela {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}appartiendra. »
fr.R: Tu n’as qu’à {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} mettre à genoux devant moi pour m’adorer, et tout sera à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. »

sw.L: Wewe, basi, ukiniabudu mbele yangu, [mamlaka] yote yatakuwa {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."
sw.B: Basi, ukiniinamia na kuniabudu, vyote hivyo vitakuwa mali {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."
sw.R: Ukipiga magoti tu na kuniabudu, vitu hivyo vyote vitakuwa {{deity_pronoun:vyako|Vyako}}."

decisions.choice: worship before me: bow down in front of me as one bows before God
alternatives: show respect as to a ruler
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow to the ground in homage. Here the devil asks for what belongs to God alone, as Jesus' answer shows (4:8).

decisions.choice: the offer: rule over the world by bowing to the devil, instead of by the way God has set
decisions.reason: God has promised David's son an everlasting kingdom (1:32-33; Psalm 2:8). The devil offers a shortcut to that rule, without obedience and suffering.

decisions.choice: You, then, (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "you" first for emphasis; Literal keeps it, and since it opens the sentence it needs no capital-pronoun setting.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Γέγραπται· Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.

records.literal_gloss: And answering the Jesus said to him, It has been written, [The] Lord the God of you you will worship and him only you will serve.

en.B: Jesus answered him, "It stands written, 'Worship the Lord your God, and serve no one but {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.'"
en.R: Jesus answered, "The Scriptures say, 'Worship the Lord your God. He is the only one you must serve.'"

es.R: Jesús respondió: «Las Escrituras dicen: “Adora al Señor tu Dios. Él es el único a quien debes servir”».

fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Il est écrit : “Adore le Seigneur ton Dieu, et ne sers personne d’autre que {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.” »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Les Écritures disent : “Adore le Seigneur ton Dieu. C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} seul que tu dois servir.” »

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:13: worship and serve God alone
decisions.reason: Moses warns Israel not to forget the LORD when they enjoy the good land, and not to follow other gods. The Hebrew has "fear" where the Greek has "worship". "Lord" stands for the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: serve: serve in worship
decisions.reason: The verb is used for the service of worship given to God (1:74; 2:37).

decisions.choice: no "Get behind me, Satan" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: adds "Get behind me, Satan, for" before "it is written"
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts do not have these words here; many later ones add them, probably from Matthew 4:10 or Mark 8:33. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Worship ... serve no one but him (B); Worship ... He is the only one you must serve (R)
alternatives: You shall worship ... and him only shall you serve
decisions.reason: The Greek future here is a command. Balanced and Readable say it as a direct command, as in Matthew 4:10.

decisions.choice: darás culto (L); servir (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means serving in worship (meaning decision m2); Literal says so with "dar culto", as in Matthew 4:10, and Balanced and Readable keep the plain "servir" as the English does.

source.text: Ἤγαγεν δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἔστησεν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν ἐντεῦθεν κάτω·

sw.L: Kisha alimpeleka Yerusalemu, akamsimamisha juu ya ncha ya hekalu, akamwambia, "Kama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni Mwana wa Mungu, jitupe chini kutoka hapa;

decisions.choice: the pinnacle of the temple: a high edge or corner of the temple buildings
alternatives: the top of the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word means "little wing", a projecting part of a building. The word for temple here covers the whole temple area, not only the sanctuary. The south-east corner of the temple courts stood high above the Kidron Valley.

decisions.choice: the third test is in Jerusalem: Luke's order ends where his Gospel goes
decisions.reason: Matthew ends with the mountain; Luke ends with Jerusalem, the city where Jesus will die and rise (9:51; 24:47).

decisions.choice: the devil
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

decisions.choice: ncha ya hekalu (L); ukingo wa juu kabisa (B)
decisions.reason: Which part of the temple is meant is not certain (meaning decision m1); "kinara" is also a lampstand or a minaret, so the drafts describe a high point or edge, as in Matthew 4:5.

source.text: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.

records.literal_gloss: it has been written for that To the angels of him he will command concerning you to guard you, \v 11 and that On hands they will lift up you, lest you strike against a stone the foot of you.

en.L: for it is written, 'He will command {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels concerning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, to guard {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},' \v 11 and, 'On [their] hands they will lift {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} up, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do not strike {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot against a stone.'"
en.B: For Scripture says, 'He will give {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels orders about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, to keep {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} safe,' \v 11 and, 'They will hold {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} up in their hands, so that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot will not strike a stone.'"
en.R: The Scriptures say, 'God will tell {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels to take care of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.' \v 11 They also say, 'The angels will catch {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in their hands, so that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not even hurt {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} foot on a rock.'"

es.L: porque está escrito: “A {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ángeles dará órdenes acerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, para que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} guarden”, \v 11 y: “Sobre [sus] manos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} llevarán, no sea que golpees {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pie contra una piedra”».

fr.B: Car l’Écriture dit : “Il donnera à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges des ordres à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} sujet, pour qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} gardent”, \v 11 et encore : “Ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} soutiendront de leurs mains, pour que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} pied ne heurte pas de pierre.” »

sw.R: Maandiko yanasema, 'Mungu atawaambia malaika {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakutunze.' \v 11 Yanasema pia, 'Malaika watakudaka kwa mikono yao, ili hata usiumize mguu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kwenye mwamba.'"

decisions.choice: Psalm 91:11-12 (90:11-12 in the Greek Old Testament): God's care for the one who trusts him
decisions.reason: The psalm promises protection to the person who takes shelter in God. The devil quotes it to push Jesus into forcing God to act. He leaves out the words "in all your ways".

decisions.choice: for it is written: the devil now argues from Scripture too
decisions.reason: After two answers from Scripture, the devil uses Scripture himself. The sentence continues the devil's words from 4:9.

decisions.choice: God (as the subject of the first line); The angels (as the subject of the second)
decisions.reason: Readable names who will do these things.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for the psalm inside the devil's words
decisions.reason: The devil's speech runs from 4:9 to the end of 4:11; the quoted lines are marked inside it.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Εἴρηται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: And answering said to him the Jesus that It has been said, Not you will test [the] Lord the God of you.

en.L: And answering, Jesus said to him, "It is said, 'You shall not test [the] Lord your God.'"
en.B: Jesus answered him, "It has been said, 'You must not test the Lord your God.'"
en.R: Jesus answered, "The Scriptures also say, 'Never try to make the Lord your God prove {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.'"

es.L: Y respondiendo, Jesús le dijo: «Está dicho: “No pondrás a prueba al Señor tu Dios”».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Se ha dicho: “No debes poner a prueba al Señor tu Dios”».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Las Escrituras también dicen: “Nunca intentes obligar al Señor tu Dios a demostrar quién es”».

fr.L: Et répondant, Jésus lui dit : « Il est dit : “Tu ne mettras pas à l’épreuve le Seigneur ton Dieu.” »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Il a été dit : “Tu ne dois pas mettre à l’épreuve le Seigneur ton Dieu.” »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Les Écritures disent aussi : “N’essaie jamais d’obliger le Seigneur ton Dieu à prouver qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est.” »

sw.L: Na Yesu akajibu, akamwambia, "Imesemwa kwamba, 'Hutamjaribu Bwana Mungu wako.'"
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Imesemwa, 'Hupaswi kumjaribu Bwana Mungu wako.'"
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Maandiko yanasema pia, 'Usijaribu kamwe kumlazimisha Bwana Mungu wako ajithibitishe.'"

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 6:16: as Israel tested God at Massah
decisions.reason: At Massah the people demanded water and asked whether the LORD was among them or not (Exodus 17:7). Jumping from the temple would demand that God prove his care. "Lord" stands for the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: it is said: Scripture has spoken and its word stands
decisions.reason: Luke varies "it is written" with "it has been said"; the sense is the same. Jesus answers Scripture misused with Scripture rightly understood.

decisions.choice: test: try to put God to the proof
decisions.reason: The verb is a stronger form of the one used for the devil's tempting (4:2).

decisions.choice: Never try to make the Lord your God prove himself
alternatives: You shall not test the Lord your God
decisions.reason: Readable says what testing God means here, as the meaning decisions explain.

source.text: καὶ συντελέσας πάντα πειρασμὸν ὁ διάβολος ἀπέστη ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι καιροῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having finished every temptation the devil departed from him until an opportune time.

en.L: And having finished every temptation, the devil departed from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} until an opportune time.
en.B: Once the devil had tried every kind of test, he left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to wait for a better moment.
en.R: When the devil had finished trying to make Jesus do wrong, he left {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for a while. He would wait for another chance.

es.L: Y habiendo acabado toda tentación, el diablo se apartó de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hasta un tiempo oportuno.
es.B: Una vez que el diablo terminó de ponerlo a prueba de todas las maneras, se apartó de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para esperar un momento más oportuno.
es.R: Cuando el diablo terminó de tratar de hacer que Jesús hiciera lo malo, se alejó de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por un tiempo. Esperaría otra oportunidad.

fr.L: Et ayant achevé toute tentation, le diable s’éloigna de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} jusqu’à un moment favorable.
fr.B: Après avoir épuisé toutes les sortes d’épreuves, le diable {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitta, en attendant un moment plus propice.
fr.R: Quand le diable a fini d’essayer de pousser Jésus à faire le mal, il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a laissé pour un temps. Il allait attendre une autre occasion.

sw.L: Na Ibilisi, akiisha kutimiza kila aina ya jaribu, aliondoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} mpaka wakati muafaka.
sw.B: Ibilisi alipokwisha kumjaribu kwa kila namna, alimwacha ili angoje nafasi nyingine iliyo bora.
sw.R: Ibilisi alipomaliza kujaribu kumshawishi Yesu atende mabaya, alimwacha kwa muda. Angesubiri nafasi nyingine.

decisions.choice: every temptation: every kind of test, not only these three
decisions.reason: Luke has told three tests as examples of the whole period (4:2).

decisions.choice: until an opportune time: until another fitting moment
decisions.reason: The devil does not give up. Luke later says that Satan entered Judas (22:3), and Jesus speaks of the hour of darkness at his arrest (22:53).

decisions.choice: for a while. He would wait for another chance.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase in two short sentences.

source.text: Καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And returned the Jesus in the power of the Spirit into the Galilee.

en.L: And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee.
en.B: Jesus went back to Galilee, and the power of the Spirit was with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus went back to Galilee, and the Holy Spirit gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} power.

es.L: Y regresó Jesús, en el poder del Espíritu, a Galilea.
es.B: Jesús regresó a Galilea, y el poder del Espíritu estaba con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús volvió a Galilea, y el Espíritu Santo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daba poder.

fr.L: Et Jésus retourna, dans la puissance de l’Esprit, en Galilée.
fr.B: Jésus retourna en Galilée, et la puissance de l’Esprit était avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus est retourné en Galilée, et l’Esprit Saint {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnait sa puissance.

sw.L: Na Yesu alirejea katika uweza wa Roho hadi Galilaya.
sw.B: Yesu alirudi Galilaya, na nguvu ya Roho ilikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}.
sw.R: Yesu alirudi Galilaya, na Roho Mtakatifu alimpa nguvu.

decisions.choice: in the power of the Spirit: the Spirit's power at work in him
decisions.reason: Luke links Jesus' work to the Spirit again and again (3:22; 4:1; 4:18). The same Spirit gives the apostles power in Acts 1:8.

decisions.choice: Galilee: the northern region, where Jesus grew up
decisions.reason: Galilee was ruled by Herod Antipas (3:1). Nazareth and Capernaum are both there.

decisions.choice: the power of the Spirit was with him (B); the Holy Spirit gave him power (R)
alternatives: in the power of the Spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the phrase into a clause. Readable says "Holy Spirit" so that young readers know which spirit is meant.

source.text: καὶ φήμη ἐξῆλθεν καθ’ ὅλης τῆς περιχώρου περὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And a report went out through all the surrounding region about him.

en.L: And a report went out through the whole surrounding region about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Word about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out through all the country around.
en.R: People everywhere in that area heard about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y una noticia salió por toda la región de alrededor acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: La noticia acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se extendió por toda la comarca.
es.R: La gente de todos los lugares de esa zona oyó hablar de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.B: On parla de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dans toute la contrée d’alentour.
fr.R: Partout dans cette région, les gens ont entendu parler de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.R: Watu kila mahali katika eneo lile walisikia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

decisions.choice: a report: what people said about him
decisions.reason: The word means talk or fame that spreads by word of mouth.

decisions.choice: People everywhere in that area heard about him
decisions.reason: Readable says the same thing from the hearers' side.

source.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδίδασκεν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν, δοξαζόμενος ὑπὸ πάντων.

records.literal_gloss: And he was teaching in the synagogues of them being glorified by all.

en.R: He taught in the synagogues, the places where Jewish people met to worship God. Everyone there spoke highly of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.R: Il enseignait dans les synagogues, les maisons où les Juifs se réunissaient pour prier Dieu. Là, tout le monde disait du bien de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akifundisha katika masinagogi yao, huku wote wakimtukuza.
sw.B: Aliendelea kufundisha katika masinagogi yao, na wote waliomsikia walimsifu.
sw.R: Alifundisha katika masinagogi, yaani nyumba ambamo Wayahudi walikutana kumwabudu Mungu. Kila mtu pale alimsifu sana.

decisions.choice: synagogues: the meeting places of Jewish communities
decisions.reason: Each town had its synagogue, where people met on the Sabbath to hear the Law and the Prophets read and explained (4:16-21). The temple, where sacrifices were offered, was only in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: being glorified by all: praised and honored by everyone
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for giving glory to God (2:20). Used of a person, it means to honor and praise. The praise here prepares for the contrast at Nazareth (4:28-29).

decisions.choice: was teaching: he taught regularly
decisions.reason: The imperfect describes his ongoing work in many places.

decisions.choice: gave him praise (B); spoke highly of him (R)
decisions.reason: "Glorified" used of a man would suggest worship. Balanced and Readable use words that fit honor given to a person, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the places where Jewish people met to worship God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word the first time it appears, as Matthew 4:23 does.

decisions.choice: sinagogas
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the Jewish meeting places (meaning decision m1); Readable explains it once, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: sinagogi, plural masinagogi
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the Jewish meeting places (meaning decision m1), in the spelling of current standard Swahili; Readable explains it once, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: huku wote wakimtukuza
decisions.reason: Literal turns the Greek passive participle into an active clause, which reads more naturally in Swahili and keeps "all" as those who glorified him.

source.text: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρά, οὗ ἦν τεθραμμένος, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν κατὰ τὸ εἰωθὸς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀναγνῶναι.

records.literal_gloss: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and he entered according to the custom to him on the day of the Sabbaths into the synagogue, and stood up to read.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to Nazareth, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been brought up, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered, according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} custom, on the day of the Sabbaths into the synagogue, and stood up to read.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to Nazareth, the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} grew up. On the Sabbath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to the synagogue, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} always did, and stood up to read the Scriptures.
en.R: Jesus went to Nazareth, the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had grown up. On the Sabbath day, as usual, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to the synagogue. There {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stood up to read from the Scriptures.

es.L: Y vino a Nazaret, donde se había criado, y entró, según {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} costumbre, el día de los sábados en la sinagoga, y se levantó a leer.
es.B: Luego llegó a Nazaret, el pueblo donde había crecido. El sábado fue a la sinagoga, como siempre lo hacía, y se puso de pie para leer las Escrituras.
es.R: Jesús fue a Nazaret, el pueblo donde había crecido. El sábado, como de costumbre, fue a la sinagoga. Allí se puso de pie para leer las Escrituras.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint à Nazareth, où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait été élevé, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra, selon {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} coutume, le jour des sabbats, dans la synagogue, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se leva pour lire.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint à Nazareth, la ville où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait grandi. Le jour du sabbat, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se rendit à la synagogue, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le faisait toujours, et se leva pour lire les Écritures.
fr.R: Jésus est allé à Nazareth, la ville où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait grandi. Le jour du sabbat, comme d’habitude, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé à la synagogue. Là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est levé pour lire les Écritures.

sw.L: Kisha alikuja Nazareti, alikolelewa, akaingia kwa mazoea {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} siku ya Sabato ndani ya sinagogi, akasimama kusoma.
sw.B: Kisha alifika Nazareti, mji alikokulia. Siku ya Sabato aliingia katika sinagogi, kama alivyozoea kufanya siku zote, akasimama ili kusoma Maandiko.
sw.R: Yesu alikwenda Nazareti, mji alimokulia. Siku ya Sabato, kama kawaida {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, alikwenda kwenye sinagogi. Huko alisimama kusoma Maandiko.

decisions.choice: according to his custom: Jesus regularly went to synagogue on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The custom is his habit of attending synagogue (4:15). As a child he was raised in the practice of the Law (2:41-42).

decisions.choice: stood up to read: a reader stood for the reading of Scripture
decisions.reason: In the synagogue service a reading from the Law was followed by one from the Prophets. Members of the community could be asked to read, and the reader stood; the teacher sat to explain (4:20).

decisions.choice: Nazareth: the SBLGNT has the short form Nazara
decisions.reason: Luke uses the form Nazara here; elsewhere he has Nazareth (1:26; 2:4). It is the same town.

decisions.choice: on the day of the Sabbaths: on the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural form of "Sabbath" is often used for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what he stood up to read, as 4:17 goes on to tell.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the long Greek sentence.

decisions.choice: el sábado
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the Sabbath; Literal keeps the Greek plural "el día de los sábados" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: le sabbat (lowercase); la synagogue (for the whole book); "le jour des sabbats" at Literal
alternatives: le jour du sabbat at Literal
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Mark: French writes the day in lowercase, as it does other days. Literal keeps the Greek plural, which means simply the Sabbath day (m4); Balanced and Readable say "le jour du sabbat".

decisions.choice: siku ya Sabato
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the Sabbath at every level; the Greek plural "day of the Sabbaths" means one Sabbath day (meaning decision m4), so Swahili uses the singular.

source.text: καὶ ἐπεδόθη αὐτῷ βιβλίον τοῦ προφήτου Ἠσαΐου καὶ ἀναπτύξας τὸ βιβλίον εὗρεν τὸν τόπον οὗ ἦν γεγραμμένον·

records.literal_gloss: And was given to him scroll of the prophet Isaiah, and having unrolled the scroll he found the place where it was written,

en.L: And [the] scroll of the prophet Isaiah was given to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and having unrolled the scroll, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found the place where it was written:
en.B: Someone handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the scroll of the prophet Isaiah. He opened it out and found the passage that says:
en.R: Someone gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the scroll with the words of the prophet Isaiah. Jesus unrolled it and found the part where Isaiah wrote:

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fue entregado [el] rollo del profeta Isaías, y desenrollando el rollo, encontró el lugar donde estaba escrito:
es.B: Alguien {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} entregó el rollo del profeta Isaías. Lo abrió y encontró el pasaje que dice:
es.R: Alguien {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dio el rollo con las palabras del profeta Isaías. Jesús lo desenrolló y encontró la parte donde Isaías había escrito:

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} fut remis [le] rouleau du prophète Isaïe, et, ayant déroulé le rouleau, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} trouva l’endroit où il était écrit :
fr.B: On {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donna le rouleau du prophète Isaïe. Il le déroula et trouva le passage où il est écrit :
fr.R: Quelqu’un {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a donné le rouleau où étaient écrites les paroles du prophète Isaïe. Jésus l’a déroulé et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a trouvé l’endroit où Isaïe avait écrit :

sw.L: Na alipewa gombo la nabii Isaya, na akiisha kulikunjua gombo, aliona mahali palipokuwa pameandikwa:
sw.B: Mtu mmoja alimpa gombo la nabii Isaya. Akalifungua, akaipata sehemu inayosema:
sw.R: Mtu fulani alimpa gombo lenye maneno ya nabii Isaya. Yesu alilikunjua, akapata sehemu ambapo Isaya aliandika:

decisions.choice: scroll: a long roll of leather or papyrus, not a bound book
decisions.reason: Books of Scripture were written on scrolls. The reader unrolled the scroll to the passage and rolled it up again afterward (4:20).

decisions.choice: he found the place: he looked for the passage, or found it as he unrolled
alternatives: the passage was set for the day
decisions.reason: Luke does not say whether the reading was chosen by Jesus or set for that Sabbath. "Found" suggests he looked for it.

decisions.choice: Someone handed him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive into an active sentence with an unnamed subject; the attendant of 4:20 may have handed it.

decisions.choice: el rollo
decisions.reason: The Greek word was a scroll, not a bound book (meaning decision m1); "libro" would make modern readers picture pages.

decisions.choice: le rouleau at every level
decisions.reason: The word names a scroll, not a bound book (m1). "Le livre" would make French readers picture pages; "le rouleau" says what Jesus held and goes with "déroula".

decisions.choice: gombo
decisions.reason: "Gombo" is a scroll, which is what the Greek word means here (meaning decision m1); "kitabu" would make readers picture a bound book.

source.text: Πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπ’ ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, ἀπέσταλκέν με κηρύξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει, κηρύξαι ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Spirit of Lord [is] upon me, because of which he anointed me to proclaim good news to poor, he has sent me to proclaim to captives release and to blind recovery of sight, to send away oppressed in release, \v 19 to proclaim year of Lord acceptable.

en.L: "[The] Spirit of [the] Lord [is] upon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to proclaim good news to [the] poor; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to proclaim release to [the] captives and recovery of sight to [the] blind, to send away [the] oppressed in release, \v 19 to proclaim [the] year of [the] Lord's favor."
en.B: "The Spirit of the Lord rests on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to bring good news to the poor. He has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to announce freedom to the captives and sight to the blind, to set the downtrodden free, \v 19 and to announce the year when the Lord shows favor."
en.R: "The Spirit of the Lord is on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He has chosen {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to tell the good news to poor people. He has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to tell prisoners that they will be set free, and to tell blind people that they will see again. He has sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to free those who are crushed by others, \v 19 and to say, 'This is the year when the Lord will show kindness to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.'"

es.L: «[El] Espíritu del Señor [está] sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha ungido para anunciar buenas noticias a [los] pobres; {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha enviado a proclamar a [los] cautivos liberación y a [los] ciegos recobro de la vista, a enviar a [los] oprimidos en libertad, \v 19 a proclamar [el] año favorable del Señor».
es.B: «El Espíritu del Señor reposa sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha ungido para llevar buenas noticias a los pobres. Me ha enviado a anunciar libertad a los cautivos y a los ciegos que volverán a ver, a dejar libres a los oprimidos, \v 19 y a anunciar el año en que el Señor se muestra favorable».
es.R: «El Espíritu del Señor está sobre {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Me ha escogido para contar la buena noticia a los pobres. Me ha enviado a decir a los presos que serán liberados, y a los ciegos que volverán a ver. Me ha enviado a liberar a los que sufren bajo el poder de otros, \v 19 y a decir: “Este es el año en que el Señor será bondadoso con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo”».

fr.L: « L’Esprit du Seigneur [est] sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a oint pour porter la bonne nouvelle aux pauvres ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé proclamer aux captifs la libération et aux aveugles le retour de la vue, renvoyer en liberté ceux qu’on a brisés, \v 19 proclamer l’année de la faveur du Seigneur. »
fr.B: « L’Esprit du Seigneur repose sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a consacré par l’onction pour apporter la bonne nouvelle aux pauvres. Il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé annoncer aux captifs leur libération et aux aveugles qu’ils retrouvent la vue, rendre la liberté à ceux qu’on écrase, \v 19 et annoncer l’année où le Seigneur montre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur. »
fr.R: « L’Esprit du Seigneur est sur {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a choisi pour annoncer la bonne nouvelle aux pauvres. Il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé dire aux prisonniers qu’ils vont être libérés, et aux aveugles qu’ils vont voir de nouveau. Il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé libérer ceux que les autres écrasent, \v 19 et dire : “Voici l’année où le Seigneur va montrer {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bonté à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple.” »

sw.L: "Roho wa Bwana [yuko] juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kwa sababu amenipaka mafuta niwaletee maskini habari njema; amenituma niwatangazie mateka kuachiliwa na vipofu kuona tena, niwapeleke walioonewa wakiwa huru, \v 19 nitangaze mwaka wa kibali wa Bwana."
sw.B: "Roho wa Bwana anakaa juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kwa kuwa amenipaka mafuta ili niwapelekee maskini habari njema. Amenituma kuwatangazia wafungwa kwamba wako huru, na vipofu kwamba wataona tena, kuwaweka huru wanaokandamizwa, \v 19 na kutangaza mwaka wa fadhili za Bwana."
sw.R: "Roho wa Bwana yuko juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Amenichagua niwaambie maskini habari njema. Amenituma niwaambie wafungwa kwamba wataachiliwa huru, na vipofu kwamba wataona tena. Amenituma niwaweke huru wale wanaoonewa na wengine, \v 19 na kusema, 'Huu ndio mwaka ambao Bwana atawaonyesha watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wema.'"

decisions.choice: Isaiah 61:1-2, with a line from Isaiah 58:6, from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek of Isaiah 61:1-2. The line "to send away the oppressed in release" comes from Isaiah 58:6, where God describes the fast he wants. The reading stops before "the day of vengeance of our God". In Isaiah the speaker is the one anointed to bring good news to Zion; Jesus says it is fulfilled in him (4:21). "Lord" stands for the divine name in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: anointed: set apart by God for a task, as kings, priests and prophets were anointed with oil
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the title Christ, "the anointed one". Jesus was anointed with the Spirit at his baptism (3:22; Acts 10:38).

decisions.choice: release: freedom, the same word as "forgiveness" in 1:77 and 3:3
decisions.reason: The word means a setting free, from debts, prison or sins. Luke uses it both for forgiveness and here for release; the two are not separated.

decisions.choice: the year of the Lord's favor: the year of release in the Law, the Jubilee
decisions.reason: In the Jubilee, every fiftieth year, release was proclaimed through the land; debts were canceled and land returned to its families (Leviticus 25:10). Isaiah uses the picture for God's coming salvation.

decisions.choice: recovery of sight to the blind: as in the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: the opening of prison to the bound, as the Hebrew of Isaiah 61:1 can be read
decisions.reason: The Hebrew line can mean release from darkness for prisoners; the Greek version, which Luke quotes, has sight for the blind. Jesus will give sight to the blind (7:21-22; 18:35-43).

decisions.choice: no "to heal the brokenhearted" (SBLGNT)
alternatives: adds "to heal the brokenhearted" after "he has sent me"
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts do not have the line; many later ones add it from Isaiah 61:1. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: me (with the capital-pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Jesus reads the words as spoken about himself (4:21), so "me" is a pronoun for Jesus, and "he" is a pronoun for God.

decisions.choice: chosen
decisions.reason: Readable says what the anointing means; Literal and Balanced keep the word, which links to "Christ".

decisions.choice: 'This is the year when the Lord will show kindness to his people.'
alternatives: to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor
decisions.reason: Readable puts the announcement into words that can be said aloud. "His people" is supplied from the context of Isaiah 61.

decisions.choice: the downtrodden
decisions.reason: The word means people who are broken or crushed.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}
decisions.reason: Jesus reads these words of himself, so the pronouns for him take the span as in the English; a sentence that begins with "Me" is capitalised either way and has none.

decisions.choice: anunciar buenas noticias (L, B); contar la buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is rendered as what it says, announcing good news; "evangelizar" now suggests a church activity, and "evangelio" is kept for the noun that names the message.

decisions.choice: m’a oint (L); m’a consacré par l’onction (B); m’a choisi (R)
decisions.reason: Anointing sets someone apart for a task (m2). Literal keeps the verb "oindre", which links to "Christ"; its forms are rare in speech, so Balanced says "consacré par l’onction", which keeps the image, and Readable says what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: le Seigneur montre {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur (B)
alternatives: l’année de la faveur du Seigneur
decisions.reason: French "montrer" needs an object, so Balanced supplies the possessive, which is a pronoun for God and carries the setting where the English has none.

decisions.choice: kuwaletea habari njema
decisions.reason: The verb is rendered as what it says, bringing good news, at every level; "Injili" is kept for the noun that names the message.

decisions.choice: amenipaka mafuta
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of anointing with oil (meaning decision m2); Readable says "amenichagua", as the English Readable says "chosen".

source.text: καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν· καὶ πάντων οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having rolled up the scroll having given back to the attendant he sat down; and of all the eyes in the synagogue were fixed on him.

en.L: And having rolled up the scroll and given [it] back to the attendant, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down; and the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He rolled the scroll up again, handed it back to the attendant, and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} seat. All the eyes in the synagogue were fixed on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Jesus closed the scroll and handed it back to the man in charge. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down. Everyone in the synagogue was staring at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y habiendo enrollado el rollo y devuelto [este] al asistente, se sentó; y los ojos de todos los [que estaban] en la sinagoga se clavaban en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Enrolló de nuevo el rollo, se lo devolvió al asistente y se sentó. Todas las miradas en la sinagoga estaban puestas en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Jesús cerró el rollo y se lo devolvió al encargado. Luego se sentó. Todos en la sinagoga {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} miraban fijamente.

fr.L: Et, ayant replié le rouleau [et l’]ayant rendu au servant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’assit ; et les yeux de tous dans la synagogue étaient fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Il referma le rouleau, le rendit au servant de la synagogue et s’assit. Dans la synagogue, tous avaient les yeux fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Jésus a refermé le rouleau et il l’a rendu à l’homme qui s’occupait de la synagogue. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’est assis. Tous les gens dans la synagogue avaient les yeux fixés sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Na akiisha kulikunja gombo na kumrudishia mhudumu, aliketi; na macho ya wote katika sinagogi yalikuwa yakimkazia.
sw.B: Alilikunja gombo tena, akamrudishia mhudumu, akaketi. Watu wote ndani ya sinagogi walikuwa wakimtazama kwa makini.
sw.R: Yesu alilifunga gombo na kumrudishia mhudumu wa sinagogi. Kisha akaketi. Kila mtu katika sinagogi alikuwa akimtazama sana.

decisions.choice: the attendant: the synagogue official who looked after the scrolls
decisions.reason: The word is used for an assistant or officer. In the synagogue he kept the sacred scrolls and handed them to the reader.

decisions.choice: he sat down: the position of a teacher about to explain the reading
alternatives: he had finished and sat down to listen
decisions.reason: Teachers sat to teach (5:3; Matthew 5:1). The people wait for him to speak.

source.text: ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: He began then to say to them that Today has been fulfilled the scripture this in the ears of you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to say to them, "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears."
en.B: He began by telling them, "Today, as you have been listening, these words of Scripture have come true."
en.R: He said to them, "What you just heard {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} read has come true today!"

es.L: Y empezó a decirles: «Hoy se ha cumplido esta Escritura en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} oídos».
es.B: Comenzó diciéndoles: «Hoy, mientras {{plural_you:ustedes escuchaban|vosotros escuchabais}}, estas palabras de la Escritura se han cumplido».
es.R: Entonces les dijo: «¡Hoy se ha cumplido lo que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:acaban|acabáis}} de oír leer!».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à leur dire : « Aujourd’hui cette Écriture a été accomplie à vos oreilles. »
fr.B: Il se mit à leur dire : « Aujourd’hui, pendant que vous écoutiez, ces paroles de l’Écriture se sont réalisées. »
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez entendu lire s’est réalisé aujourd’hui ! »

sw.L: Naye akaanza kuwaambia kwamba, "Leo andiko hili limetimizwa katika masikio yenu."
sw.B: Alianza kwa kuwaambia, "Leo, mlipokuwa mkisikiliza, maneno haya ya Maandiko yametimia."
sw.R: Aliwaambia, "Yale mliyonisikia nikisoma yametimia leo!"

decisions.choice: today ... fulfilled: what Isaiah announced is happening now, in Jesus
alternatives: it will be fulfilled one day
decisions.reason: The perfect tense "has been fulfilled" means the fulfillment has taken place and stands. "Today" is a key word in Luke (2:11; 19:9; 23:43).

decisions.choice: in your ears: as you heard it
alternatives: the Scripture is fulfilled by your hearing it
decisions.reason: The phrase means "in your hearing": the reading they have just heard is coming true before them.

decisions.choice: as you have been listening (B); What you just heard me read (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. "Me" in Readable is Jesus speaking of himself.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}}, {{plural_you:ustedes escuchaban|vosotros escuchabais}}
decisions.reason: Every plural "you", pronoun or verb, is the plural_you setting: the ustedes form by default, the vosotros form as the alternative.

source.text: καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος;

records.literal_gloss: And all were bearing witness to him and were marveling at the words of the grace coming out of the mouth of him, and they were saying, Not son is of Joseph this?

en.L: And all were bearing witness to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and marveling at the words of grace coming out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth, and they were saying, "Is this not [the] son of Joseph?"
en.B: Everyone there was speaking in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} favor, and they wondered at the words of grace that came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. And they kept saying, "Is this not Joseph's son?"
en.R: Everyone said good things about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They were amazed that such kind and beautiful words came from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth. They said, "Is this not Joseph's son?"

es.L: Y todos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daban testimonio, y se asombraban ante las palabras de la gracia que brotaban de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca, y decían: «¿Acaso no es este [el] hijo de José?».
es.B: Todos hablaban a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} favor y se admiraban de las palabras llenas de gracia que salían de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca. Y decían una y otra vez: «¿No es este el hijo de José?».
es.R: Todos decían cosas buenas de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Estaban asombrados de que de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} boca salieran palabras tan amables y hermosas. Decían: «¿No es este el hijo de José?».

fr.L: Et tous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendaient témoignage et s’étonnaient des paroles de grâce qui sortaient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche, et ils disaient : « Celui-ci n’est-il pas [le] fils de Joseph ? »
fr.B: Tous parlaient en {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} faveur et s’émerveillaient des paroles pleines de grâce qui sortaient de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche. Et ils répétaient : « N’est-ce pas le fils de Joseph ? »
fr.R: Tout le monde disait du bien de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Les gens s’étonnaient d’entendre sortir de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} bouche des paroles si belles et si pleines de bonté. Ils disaient : « Ce n’est pas le fils de Joseph, celui-là ? »

sw.L: Na wote walikuwa wakitoa ushuhuda juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na kushangaa kwa ajili ya maneno ya neema yaliyotoka katika kinywa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, nao walikuwa wakisema, "Je, huyu si mwana wa Yusufu?"
sw.B: Kila mtu pale alimsema vizuri, na walishangazwa na maneno ya neema yaliyotoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Wakawa wakisema, "Je, huyu si mwana wa Yusufu?"
sw.R: Wote walisema mambo mazuri juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Walishangaa kwamba maneno mazuri na ya upole kiasi hicho yalitoka kinywani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Wakasema, "Je, huyu si mwana wa Yusufu?"

decisions.choice: words of grace: gracious words, full of charm and kindness, and speaking of God's favor
decisions.reason: The noun is the usual word for grace. With "words" it describes speech that is pleasing and kind (Colossians 4:6). The words were also about God's favor to the poor and captive (4:18-19). Literal and Balanced keep "grace"; Readable gives the sense the hearers felt.

decisions.choice: were bearing witness to him: they spoke well of him
decisions.reason: With this construction the verb means to speak in favor of someone. The mood changes only after Jesus' reply (4:28).

decisions.choice: Is this not the son of Joseph?: they expect the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question is surprise that a local man, whose family they know, speaks like this. Luke has said that Jesus was thought to be Joseph's son (3:23).

decisions.choice: such kind and beautiful words
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the phrase, as the meaning decision on the word explains.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· Ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν· ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Surely you will say to me the proverb this, Physician, heal yourself; what we heard having happened in the Capernaum do also here in the hometown of you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Surely you will say to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} this proverb: 'Physician, heal {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}! What we heard was done in Capernaum, do here also in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hometown.'"
en.B: He said to them, "No doubt you will quote this saying to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: 'Doctor, cure {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}!' And you will tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, 'Do here in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own town the things we heard {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did in Capernaum.'"
en.R: Jesus said to them, "I am sure you will tell {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the old saying, 'Doctor, first make {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} well!' You will say, 'We heard about what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did in Capernaum. Do the same things here in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own hometown!'"

es.L: Y les dijo: «Seguramente {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:citarán|citaréis}} este proverbio: “Médico, sánate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo; todo lo que oímos que pasó en Cafarnaúm, hazlo también aquí en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} patria”».
es.B: Les dijo: «Sin duda {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:van|vais}} a citar este dicho: “¡Doctor, cúrate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo!”. Y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “Haz aquí, en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propia tierra, lo que oímos que hiciste en Cafarnaúm”».
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «Estoy seguro de que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}} el viejo dicho: “Doctor, ¡primero sánate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo!”. También {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:dirán|diréis}}: “Oímos lo que hiciste en Cafarnaúm. ¡Haz lo mismo aquí, en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propio pueblo!”».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Assurément vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} direz ce proverbe : “Médecin, guéris-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} {{deity_pronoun:toi-m|Toi-m}}ême ! Tout ce que nous avons appris qui s’est passé à Capharnaüm, fais[-le] aussi ici, dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} patrie.” »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Sans doute allez-vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} citer ce dicton : “Médecin, guéris-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} {{deity_pronoun:toi-m|Toi-m}}ême !” Et vous {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} direz : “Ce que nous avons appris que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait à Capharnaüm, fais-le donc ici aussi, dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} propre ville.” »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Je suis sûr que vous allez {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dire le vieux proverbe : “Médecin, commence par {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} soigner {{deity_pronoun:toi-m|Toi-m}}ême !” Vous allez dire : “Nous avons entendu parler de ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait à Capharnaüm. Fais la même chose ici, dans la ville où {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as grandi !” »

sw.L: Na akawaambia, "Kwa hakika mtaniambia methali hii: 'Mganga, jitibu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}! Mambo yote tuliyosikia yamefanyika Kapernaumu, yafanye pia hapa katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa nyumbani.'"
sw.B: Aliwaambia, "Bila shaka mtanitajia msemo huu: 'Daktari, jitibu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!' Tena mtaniambia, 'Yafanye hapa katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa nyumbani yale tuliyosikia ulifanya Kapernaumu.'"
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia, "Najua mtaniambia ule msemo wa zamani, 'Daktari, kwanza jiponye {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!' Mtasema, 'Tumesikia mambo uliyofanya Kapernaumu. Fanya mambo hayo hayo hapa katika mji {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa nyumbani!'"

decisions.choice: Physician, heal yourself: prove what you claim by doing it for your own people
alternatives: a mocking call to cure his own illness
decisions.reason: A doctor who cannot heal himself is not trusted. Here the saying means: do your wonders here at home, among your own, and then we will believe.

decisions.choice: what we heard was done in Capernaum ...: still the words Jesus expects them to say
decisions.reason: The second part spells out what the proverb means for them, so it stands inside the quotation.

decisions.choice: what was done in Capernaum: works not yet told in Luke
decisions.reason: Luke tells the Capernaum events after this (4:31-41). The words assume Jesus had already worked there (4:14-15).

decisions.choice: Doctor
decisions.reason: "Doctor" is the everyday word; Literal keeps "Physician".

decisions.choice: And you will tell me (B); You will say (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark that the second part is still what the people will say.

decisions.choice: Médecin at every level
decisions.reason: English Balanced and Readable say "Doctor" because "physician" is formal. French "médecin" is the everyday word, and the proverb is known in French in this form; "Docteur" is a way of addressing a doctor, not the name of the trade.

decisions.choice: mganga (L); daktari (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Mganga" is the older Swahili word for anyone who heals; Balanced and Readable use "daktari", as the English says "Doctor". The proverb means: prove your claims among your own people (meaning decision m1).

source.text: εἶπεν δέ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: He said then, Truly I say to you that no prophet acceptable is in the hometown of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Truly I tell you, no prophet is acceptable in his hometown.
en.B: He added, "Truly I tell you, a prophet is never welcome in his own hometown.
en.R: Then Jesus said, "I tell you the truth, the people of a prophet's own town never welcome him.

es.L: Y dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ningún profeta es aceptado en su tierra.
es.B: Luego dijo: «En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a ningún profeta lo reciben bien en su propio pueblo.
es.R: Después Jesús dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: la gente del pueblo de un profeta nunca lo recibe bien.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « En vérité, je vous le dis : aucun prophète n’est bien reçu dans sa patrie.
fr.B: Il ajouta : « En vérité, je vous le dis, un prophète n’est jamais bien accueilli dans sa propre ville.
fr.R: Puis Jésus a dit : « Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : les gens de la ville d’un prophète ne l’accueillent jamais bien.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Kweli nawaambia kwamba hakuna nabii aliye na kibali katika mji wa kwao.
sw.B: Aliongeza, "Kweli nawaambia, nabii hakaribishwi kamwe katika mji wa kwao.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alisema, "Nawaambia ukweli, watu wa mji wa nabii mwenyewe hawamkaribishi kamwe.

decisions.choice: Truly: a Hebrew word (amen) that confirms what follows
decisions.reason: Elsewhere "amen" agrees with what has just been said. Jesus uses it to introduce his own words with authority. This is the first time in Luke.

decisions.choice: acceptable: welcomed, received with favor
decisions.reason: It is the same word as "favor" in "the year of the Lord's favor" (4:19). The Lord's year of welcome is announced, but the prophet himself is not welcomed at home.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering, as in John.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's single "amen" (meaning decision m1), the same in every Gospel.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R) (for the whole book)
alternatives: Je vous le dis en vérité
decisions.reason: As the term sheet and Mark. "Amen" at the start of a saying is not French usage; the set phrase keeps the solemn opening at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's single "amen" (meaning decision m1), the same in every Gospel.

source.text: ἐπ’ ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἠλίου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ἐπὶ ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν, καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἠλίας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.

records.literal_gloss: In truth then I say to you, many widows were in the days of Elijah in the Israel, when was shut the heaven for years three and months six, as came a famine great upon all the land, \v 26 and to none of them was sent Elijah except to Zarephath of the Sidon to a woman widow.

en.L: But in truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months, when a great famine came over all the land, \v 26 and Elijah was sent to none of them except to Zarephath of Sidon, to a woman [who was] a widow.
en.B: But I tell you in truth: in Elijah's day, when the sky stayed shut for three years and six months and a great famine struck the whole land, Israel had many widows. \v 26 Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to a widow at Zarephath in the land of Sidon.
en.R: Here is the truth. In the time of Elijah no rain fell for three and a half years, and there was very little food anywhere in the land. Israel had many widows then. \v 26 But God did not send Elijah to any of them. Instead, God sent him to a widow in the town of Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, outside Israel.

es.L: Pero de verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: había muchas viudas en los días de Elías en Israel, cuando el cielo quedó cerrado durante tres años y seis meses, al sobrevenir un hambre grande sobre toda la tierra, \v 26 y Elías no fue enviado a ninguna de ellas, excepto a Sarepta de Sidón, a una mujer [que era] viuda.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo con toda verdad: en tiempos de Elías, cuando el cielo permaneció cerrado tres años y seis meses y un hambre terrible azotó todo el país, había en Israel muchas viudas. \v 26 Sin embargo, Elías no fue enviado a ninguna de ellas, sino a una viuda de Sarepta, en la región de Sidón.
es.R: Esta es la verdad. En tiempos de Elías no llovió durante tres años y medio, y casi no había comida en ninguna parte del país. En ese tiempo había muchas viudas en Israel. \v 26 Pero Dios no envió a Elías a ninguna de ellas. En cambio, Dios lo envió a una viuda del pueblo de Sarepta, en la tierra de Sidón, fuera de Israel.

fr.L: Mais en vérité je vous le dis : il y avait beaucoup de veuves en Israël aux jours d’Élie, quand le ciel a été fermé pendant trois ans et six mois, quand une grande famine est survenue sur tout le pays, \v 26 et Élie n’a été envoyé vers aucune d’elles, sinon à Sarepta de Sidon, vers une femme veuve.
fr.B: Mais je vous le dis en vérité : au temps d’Élie, quand le ciel est resté fermé trois ans et six mois et qu’une grande famine a frappé tout le pays, il y avait beaucoup de veuves en Israël. \v 26 Pourtant, Élie n’a été envoyé chez aucune d’elles, mais chez une veuve de Sarepta, dans le pays de Sidon.
fr.R: Voici la vérité. À l’époque d’Élie, il n’a pas plu pendant trois ans et demi, et il n’y avait presque plus rien à manger dans tout le pays. Il y avait alors beaucoup de veuves en Israël. \v 26 Mais Dieu n’a envoyé Élie chez aucune d’elles. Il l’a envoyé chez une veuve de la ville de Sarepta, dans le pays de Sidon, en dehors d’Israël.

sw.L: Lakini nawaambia kwa kweli, kulikuwa na wajane wengi siku za Eliya katika Israeli, wakati anga lilipofungwa kwa miaka mitatu na miezi sita, njaa kuu ilipotokea juu ya nchi nzima, \v 26 na Eliya hakupelekwa kwa hata mmoja wao, ila Sarepta ya Sidoni, kwa mwanamke [aliyekuwa] mjane.
sw.B: Lakini nawaambia hakika: katika siku za Eliya, anga lilipokaa limefungwa kwa miaka mitatu na miezi sita, na njaa kali ikaikumba nchi yote, Israeli ilikuwa na wajane wengi. \v 26 Hata hivyo Eliya hakutumwa kwa yeyote kati yao, bali kwa mjane mmoja wa Sarepta katika nchi ya Sidoni.
sw.R: Huu ndio ukweli. Wakati wa Eliya mvua haikunyesha kwa miaka mitatu na nusu, na chakula kilikuwa haba sana kila mahali nchini. Wakati huo Israeli ilikuwa na wajane wengi. \v 26 Lakini Mungu hakumtuma Eliya kwa yeyote kati yao. Badala yake, Mungu alimtuma kwa mjane mmoja katika mji wa Sarepta, katika nchi ya Sidoni, nje ya Israeli.

decisions.choice: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath: 1 Kings 17:8-24
decisions.reason: During the drought God sent Elijah to a widow in Zarephath, a town of Sidon, outside Israel. She fed him, and he raised her son. Jesus' point is that God sent his prophet to a foreigner rather than to Israel.

decisions.choice: three years and six months: the length of the drought in Jewish tradition
alternatives: the third year, as in 1 Kings 18:1
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 18:1 says the rain came "in the third year". James 5:17 also gives three years and six months; the times may be counted from different starting points.

decisions.choice: the sky was shut: no rain fell
alternatives: the heavens were closed to prayer
decisions.reason: The sky is pictured as a store of rain that God closes (Deuteronomy 11:17; 1 Kings 8:35).

decisions.choice: in truth: truly, I am telling you something sure
decisions.reason: The phrase strengthens the statement, like "truly" in 4:24.

decisions.choice: God did not send ... God sent him
decisions.reason: Readable names who sent Elijah, which the passive implies.

decisions.choice: outside Israel
